topic.name: Calculating the Magnitude of Cartesian Vectors in 2D

question.text: If $\mathbf{a} = \langle-3, 5\rangle$, then what is the magnitude of $\mathbf{a}?$

topic.name: Calculating the Magnitude of Cartesian Vectors in 2D

example.title: Calculating the Magnitude of a Vector Given in Component Form

question.explanation:
We have

\begin{align*} &\overrightarrow{OC} = \mathbf{c} =0 \mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j}, \\[3pt] &\overrightarrow{OD} = \mathbf{d} = 4\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j}. \end{align*}

Expressing $\overrightarrow{CD}$ as the difference of position vectors, we obtain:

\begin{align*} \overrightarrow{CD} &= \overrightarrow{OD}-\overrightarrow{OC}\\[3pt] &= \mathbf{d} - \mathbf{c} \\[3pt] &= (4\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j}) - ( 2\mathbf{j})\\[3pt] &=4 \mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j} \end{align*}

Now, using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

\begin{align*} |\overrightarrow{CD}| &= \sqrt{4^2+(-3)^2} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{16+9} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{25}\\[3pt] &=5. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating a Vector From Position Vectors and then Computing its Magnitude

question.text: Points $C$ and $D$ are shown in the picture above. Find $|\overrightarrow{CD}|.$
question.explanation:
From the picture, we obtain $C(-3,4)$ and $D(2,3).$ So, we have

\begin{align*} &\overrightarrow{OC} = \mathbf{c} = -3\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j}, \\[3pt] &\overrightarrow{OD} = \mathbf{d} = 2\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j}. \end{align*}

Expressing $\overrightarrow{CD}$ as the difference of position vectors, we obtain:

\begin{align*} \overrightarrow{CD} &= \overrightarrow{OD}-\overrightarrow{OC}\\[3pt] &= \mathbf{d} - \mathbf{c} \\[3pt] &= \left(2\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j}\right) - (-3\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j})\\[3pt] &= 5\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} \end{align*}

Now, using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

\begin{align*} |\overrightarrow{CD}| &= \sqrt{5^2+(-1)^2} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{25+1}\\[3pt] &= \sqrt{26}. \end{align*}
